claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid and homogeneously mixed.
Surface segregation of Cu governs the early onset and progression of premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu is the lowest-melting component of the FeNiCrCoCu alloy.
The relatively low melting point of Cu drives Cu atoms to migrate toward the nanoparticle surface at elevated temperature.
Cu enrichment at the nanoparticle surface lowers the local melting temperature.
The Cu-induced local melting-point depression initiates a liquid-like surface layer before bulk melting.
The liquid-like surface layer acts as a nucleation site for further melting.
Formation of the surface liquid layer accelerates inward propagation of melting from the exterior to the nanoparticle core.
The proposed controlled comparison is between FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles and compositionally similar FeNiCrCo nanoparticles lacking Cu.
Approximately 0.8–1.0 times the bulk melting temperature represents the relevant premelting and melting regime for the nanoparticles.
Defined high-temperature dwell times permit diffusion during the experiment.
FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will exhibit a liquid-like surface layer that is absent or delayed in the Cu-free control.
FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will have a lower melting-onset temperature than FeNiCrCo nanoparticles under identical heating conditions.
The Cu-free baseline will show no early surface melting or premature phase transition under the same heating conditions.
Using an inert or ultrahigh-vacuum environment eliminates oxidation and other extrinsic effects.
Holding particle size and heating rate constant is intended to isolate the effect of Cu.
Particle size, initial homogeneity, and heating history can strongly affect the Cu-induced temperature depression and Cu diffusion kinetics.
Failure to observe both a lower melting onset and Cu surface enrichment would count against Cu segregation as the trigger of the early transition.
